tasks.objective: Give MemoryStore an injectable ID source and clock. Add keyword-only args id_source (callable returning str) and clock (callable returning an aware datetime) to MemoryStore.__init__ in src/neural_node_swarm/memory.py; append() takes event_id from id_source() and recorded_at from clock().isoformat(). Defaults keep current callers working: the clock defaults to datetime.now(timezone.utc) and the default ID source must give distinct IDs even when the clock is frozen (e.g. evt-<uuid4 hex>, never the timestamp). Before writing, append() raises ValueError on an event_id already stored, for JSONL (check existing events) and storage backends (check get_event in MemoryStore, and make SQLiteStorage.append_event raise ValueError on an existing ID); nothing is written. Test with a frozen clock and both backends.
success_criteria: With an injected id_source and clock, events carry exactly the injected event_id and recorded_at, on both the JSONL and SQLite backends
Two appends under a frozen clock with the default ID source get distinct event IDs
An id_source that repeats an ID makes the second append raise ValueError on both backends, and events() still holds only the first event
The new test file fails on the starting commit and the full suite passes after the change
constraints: Edit only src/neural_node_swarm/memory.py and src/neural_node_swarm/sqlite_storage.py plus one new test file, e.g. tests/test_deterministic_ids.py; other tasks this wave edit verifier.py, pyproject.toml and add new modules
Keep MemoryStore(path) and MemoryStore(storage=...) working unchanged so the CLI, orchestrator and existing tests pass

The subprocess test must fail on the starting commit.

tasks.objective: Add a narrow task with known ground truth and a deterministic verifier in a new module src/neural_node_swarm/task_verifier.py. Task: sum_objective([2, 3, 5]) returns the start objective "Sum: 2,3,5"; expected_answer(objective) parses it and returns the exact target string "Answer: 10". verify_task_output(start_objective, output) first runs verify_node_output and rejects malformed outputs, then passes only if output["objective"] equals expected_answer(start_objective); it returns a dict with status "passed" or "rejected" and named checks. verify_relay(start_objective, final_output) judges an Orchestrator.run result the same way. Tests: a correct three-round node driven by Orchestrator.run over a tmp JSONL MemoryStore passes; negative controls that verify_node_output accepts but the task verifier rejects: a wrong sum, an off-by-one sum, extra text after the answer, the DisposableNode relay that never answers, and a correct answer for different numbers.
success_criteria: A correct relay run through Orchestrator.run is judged passed by verify_relay
Each negative control is accepted by verify_node_output but rejected by verify_task_output, with a failing check named for the task answer
Malformed outputs (e.g. carrying a notes field) are rejected by the task verifier
The verifier is deterministic: no model calls, network, randomness or clock
The new test file fails on the starting commit and the full suite passes after the change
constraints: Only add src/neural_node_swarm/task_verifier.py and one new test file, e.g. tests/test_task_verifier.py; do not edit any existing file, including __init__.py, verifier.py, memory.py and pyproject.toml
